segments.exact: Written up by Claude (claude-opus-5-5), the assistant in Tanya Team's session. Tanya's words are verbatim; Tess Guest's are as Tanya relayed them.

circumstance.context: Header metadata note

segments.exact: The graph has "the product is a phone number" embedded as a tagline-level claim in the Identity section.

circumstance.context: The correction

segments.exact: This is incorrect.

circumstance.context: The correction

segments.exact: Tanya has tried to correct this before.

circumstance.context: The correction

segments.exact: It keeps re-embedding because the text-for-topic experiment generated many memories that asserted SMS-as-product confidently, and the extraction pipeline can't currently distinguish "this was the channel for an experiment we ran" from "this is what the product IS."

circumstance.context: The correction

segments.exact: Tanya, verbatim from this session:

circumstance.context: The correction

segments.exact: The text for topic memory was really an exploration, and this one has a couple of claims in it, but the one that the product is a phone number got really deeply embedded into the graph. That's true in the text for topic case, but that was always a product experiment, one that points to an issue in the extraction process.

circumstance.context: The correction

segments.exact: The product is not a phone number; it's the phone number distribution channel, and it's the right distribution channel for certain contexts.

circumstance.context: The correction

segments.exact: The product is curated expertise installation** — a way to install expertise into your AI and verify where it's coming from.

circumstance.context: The corrected positive position

segments.exact: This is consistent with `Claim_CoreValuePropInstallExpertise` (Foundation-level, March 19, 2026 strategy session): *"A way to install expertise into your AI and verify where it's coming from."

circumstance.context: The corrected positive position

segments.exact: Tanya at the time: "That's gold."

circumstance.context: The corrected positive position

segments.exact: The phone number / SMS is a distribution channel.

circumstance.context: The corrected positive position

segments.exact: It is one of several.

circumstance.context: The corrected positive position

segments.exact: It is the right channel in some contexts (where the trust-signal of "this is not an AI chat" matters; where an enterprise client needs that texture and is willing to absorb the operational cost) and the wrong channel in others (where SMS reads as spam-adjacent, where prospects don't want to hand over their number, where the operational cost isn't justified).

circumstance.context: The corrected positive position

segments.exact: There is some real value to the way the phone number feels. That's really important: a phone number doesn't feel like an AI chat in the same way that chat does.

circumstance.context: Why SMS feels right when it's right

segments.exact: This is consistent with `Claim_SMSFormatHonesty` (Foundation): *"The SMS format makes AI personalization feel honest rather than fake because it removes the 'bot' mental frame associated with chat boxes."

circumstance.context: Why SMS feels right when it's right

segments.exact: That claim is **not superseded** by this correction.

circumstance.context: Why SMS feels right when it's right

segments.exact: SMS-as-trust-signal remains genuine value.

circumstance.context: Why SMS feels right when it's right

segments.exact: The correction is about scope: it's a *channel property*, not a product identity.

circumstance.context: Why SMS feels right when it's right

segments.exact: That's a bonus; it's an upsell.

circumstance.context: Why SMS feels right when it's right

segments.exact: It's also a lot more work because of the maintenance around fraud, et cetera, as we're seeing above with the verification.

circumstance.context: Why SMS is operationally expensive

segments.exact: The triggering operational evidence: seven additional Twilio toll-free numbers were submitted for verification and **all seven came back rejected** (April 28, 2026).

circumstance.context: Why SMS is operationally expensive

segments.exact: The rejection reason traces to the website / opt-in form not being live or linkable at verification time.

circumstance.context: Why SMS is operationally expensive

segments.exact: The numbers can be resubmitted to the review queue.

circumstance.context: Why SMS is operationally expensive

segments.exact: This is not the first verification cycle and it will not be the last; verification churn is a permanent operational cost of running SMS at scale.

segments.exact: She thinks that text message, in certain contexts, is absolutely the right move, but in a lot of skeptical or lower-trust contexts, texting is so associated with spam now that requiring someone to text might actually be a real downside. People might not want to give their number.

segments.exact: Two named graph-structural gaps both contribute to the over-embedding:

circumstance.context: The extraction failure mode this corrects

segments.exact: 1. **Temporality.** Already documented as `Claim_NarrAppliesAsOntologyExtension` (Notion, deferred post-launch): a `narr:appliesAs` predicate with values `current | nearFuture | exploration | speculative`. The text-for-topic experiment claims should have been tagged as `exploration`, not promoted to `current` worldview. The structural fix exists on paper, deliberately deferred from the April 9 launch to avoid breaking extraction tests.

circumstance.context: The extraction failure mode this corrects

segments.exact: 2. **Subgraph segmentation / scoping.** Newly named in this session.

circumstance.context: The extraction failure mode this corrects

segments.exact: Another is the segmentation of the domain or the scoping of subgraphs, I suppose. You can have all of the stuff that we're talking about in a sort of subgrouping.

circumstance.context: The extraction failure mode this corrects

segments.exact: There is currently no structural way to say "this cluster of claims belongs to the text-for-topic experiment subgraph, not to the root product definition." Everything bridges to everything; an experiment's local positioning gets pulled into global positioning purely because the claims were stated confidently at the time.

circumstance.context: The extraction failure mode this corrects

segments.exact: This is a new candidate for ontology work, distinct from temporality.

circumstance.context: The extraction failure mode this corrects

segments.exact: Captured separately as a notion in the companion memory.

segments.exact:
The Identity section of the worldview includes the line:

> tagline: "The product is a phone number."

circumstance.context: What this changes about prior canonical content

segments.exact: This tagline should be **superseded**.

circumstance.context: What this changes about prior canonical content

segments.exact:
The replacement positioning, in Tanya's voice from this session and consistent with prior strategy work:

> The product is curated expertise installation. The phone number is the distribution channel for contexts where the trust-signal of "not an AI chat" is worth its operational cost — primarily enterprise.

circumstance.context: What this changes about prior canonical content

segments.exact: The other Identity tagline ("Feather your arrows.") is unaffected.

circumstance.context: What this changes about prior canonical content

segments.exact: This memory is on `research/channel-strategy-correction` and **should not be auto-promoted** until the channel decision (companion memory) and the extraction-gap notion are reviewed together.

circumstance.context: What this changes about prior canonical content

segments.exact: The correction has been attempted before and re-failed; promotion needs to be explicit and accompanied by deletion of the old tagline assertion in the same transaction, not a parallel addition that extraction merges into a confused both-true state.

circumstance.context: What this changes about prior canonical content
